questions.prompt: In Separation of Concerns, which statement best describes HTTP-specific logic?
options: Connect this syllabus point to Separation of Concerns: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.
questions.answer_key: Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.
questions.explanation: Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Separation of Concerns?
options: Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
Separate HTTP handling from business rules, persistence, and integration clients. Dependency injection and consistent contracts make modules easier to test; avoid abstractions that hide control flow.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
questions.answer_key: Separate HTTP handling from business rules, persistence, and integration clients. Dependency injection and consistent contracts make modules easier to test; avoid abstractions that hide control flow.
questions.explanation: Separate HTTP handling from business rules, persistence, and integration clients. Dependency injection and consistent contracts make modules easier to test; avoid abstractions that hide control flow.

questions.prompt: A change related to Separation of Concerns appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
